articles.title: Korea Box Office: Anime Hit ‘Chiikawa’ Retains Lead as Brad Pitt Thriller ‘Heart of the Beast’ Debuts
articles.summary: Japanese animated phenomenon “Chiikawa the Movie: The Secret of the Mermaid Island” held the No. 1 position at the South Korean box office over the weekend of Oct. 30–Nov. 1, securing its third consecutive weekend atop the rankings.
body: Sony Pictures and TriStar’s survival thriller “ Heart of the Beast ” opened in second place, pulling in $1.2 million from 162,790 admissions across 1,106 screens to capture 23% of theatrical revenue. Since opening mid-week on Oct. 28, the title has accumulated $1.5 million from 215,237 admissions.

By4M Studio and Barunson E&A’s workplace comedy “Ugly Duckling Ms. Maeng” debuted in third place, taking in $326,609 from 44,799 admissions across 677 screens for 6.09% of the market. The directorial debut of screenwriter Lee Yong-jae stars Lee Sun-bin, Yoo Jae-myung, Kim Young-min, and Jeon Seok-ho, following a high school language teacher unexpectedly sequestered into the top-secret 40-day test-writing committee for the national college entrance examination. Following its premiere at the Busan International Film Festival and an Oct. 28 commercial bow, the comedy has grossed $505,208 from 71,767 viewers.

articles.title: Japanese Drifter’s Road Trip to Korea Drives Uchiyama Takuya’s ‘The Blue Breaks’ at Tokyo Gap-Financing Market
articles.summary: A man conceived through sperm donation, unsure of his place in the world, sets out on a journey to Korea in “The Blue Breaks,” an adaptation of Machiya Ryohei’s 2016 novel by Japanese filmmaker Uchiyama Takuya (“Numb”).
body: He later meets Toko, a young woman who is terminally ill but carries herself lightly, smoking and smiling despite the little time she has left. Her outlook gradually leaves its mark on him. Eventually Shukichi and the people around him travel to Korea together, where they reckon with one another’s lives and deaths.

Uchiyama, who has previously written his own screenplays from personal experience, said he felt drawn to the book in part because it was published in the year he started making films, and because Machiya wrote it at the age Uchiyama is now.

“Shukichi, the protagonist, struggles with the part of himself that never quite became ‘manly.’ I’ve also spent much of my life feeling uncomfortable with what society expects a man to be,” Uchiyama said.
He described the characters as people whose lives look very different from one another’s, and said Japan still expects everyone to be alike.

articles.title: Director Michael Mann accidentally shoots himself in the leg at gun range
articles.summary: Mann taken to hospital with superficial injury after weapon accidentally discharged while holstered. Hollywood director Michael Mann has been taken to the hospital following an apparently accidental shooting at a Los Angeles gun range, according to the Associated Press.
body: Mann, 83, reportedly shot himself in the leg while at the The Range LA. The news was first reported on celebrity website TMZ. He sustained what his representative described as a superficial injury after a weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

The Los Angeles Police Department told the Hollywood Reporter that officers had responded to The Range LA at around 4pm. “Responding units’ investigation determined the shooting to be accidental. The subject was transported to a local hospital in stable condition,” a LAPD spokesperson said.

Mann is one of the best known long-standing directors in Hollywood, known for major works like Manhunter, The Last of the Mohicans and Heat. His most recent move was Ferrari, starring Adam Driver and Penelope Cruz, that was released in 2023. Mann also helped created the hit 1980s TV cop show Miami Vice.
TMZ reported that Mann had been trying to holster his weapon when the gun accidentally discharged. Emergency services were then called and he was taken to a hospital.
points: Mann taken to hospital with superficial injury after weapon accidentally discharged while holstered.

articles.title: ‘Gintama: Yoshiwara in Flames’ Director and Producer Discuss Bringing the Cult Anime to the Big Screen
articles.summary: “Gintama: Yoshiwara in Flames” – the latest iteration of the “Gintama” story – previewed this week at Lucca Comics and Games, Europe’s largest Comic-Con, prior to a theatrical release in Italy. Variety spoke with director Naoya Andô and producer Ryo Nakamuray about their continuation of the saga.
body: The manga became a long-running 367-episode anime series and has had three previous big-screen spin-offs. “Gintama: Yoshiwara in Flames” is the fourth cinema outing for the series.

How did you want to approach this franchise without losing its soul but at the same time making it suitably cinematic? Naoya Andô: When we started planning this film, we already knew that there would be many action scenes. We were keen to use the CinemaScope ultrawide ratio as well as using 3D in order to be able to move the camera more, and give us more variety, as well as keep the camera a little distant from the subjects so we could frame the shots better and really appreciate the design and setting. It’s for this reason we made this choice.

This story was already told in the TV series but despite the title Yoshiwara didn’t burn. But here we see it burn really. Naoya Andô: Our producer Takashi Maekawa also worked on the television series and so I asked him, are we going to actually burn the town this time? And the producer said: “Yes this time we’re going to burn everything.” And so we had talked among ourselves about how we were going to do it and the group made a creative decision to do it.

articles.title: Josh Hartnett's Twisty Neo-Noir Thriller With Bruce Willis Is Streaming For Free
articles.summary: Josh Hartnett has said he had a great time working opposite stars like Bruce Willis on this wild neo-noir thriller, which is currently streaming for free.
body: Josh Hartnett once starred in a darkly comedic neo-noir thriller, and you can stream it for free at this very moment. Co-starring the action legend Bruce Willis as part of an impressive ensemble, "Lucky Number Slevin" didn't get its flowers back in 2006, but it's since garnered a loyal following. /Film editor Ben Pearson even counts it among his favorite movies of all time.

Streaming now on Tubi and Pluto TV, "Lucky Number Slevin" was directed by Paul McGuigan, whom Hartnett had previously worked with on 2004's "Wicker Park." The movie focuses on a case of mistaken identity, which puts a man named Slevin (Hartnett) in the middle of a war between two rival New York crime lords. Under the watchful eyes of Detective Brikowski (Stanley Tucci) and an assassin named Goodkat (Willis), Slevin must devise a plan to save his skin as these forces converge around him.

articles.title: Leonard Nimoy's 5 Best Cameo Appearances, Ranked
articles.summary: Whether Leonard Nimoy was playing a villain of the week or himself in animated form, he made a lot of great supporting appearances in his career.
body: Leonard Nimoy accrued his first screen credit in 1951, playing a small part in one of the vignettes in Arthur Lubin's "Queen for a Day." He then landed a leading role in the 1952 film noir "Kid Monk Beroni" (playing the title character) and appeared in the Republic serial "Zombies from the Stratosphere." It was on TV, though, that his early career really thrived, and he turned up in many, many hit shows of the day, including several Westerns. Few, for instance, remember the time Nimoy was on "Tombstone Territory." He similarly guest-starred on the forgotten "The Man from Sheanadoah" and even popped up at one point opposite Clint Eastwood on "Rawhide."

The point being: Nimoy may be best known for playing the half-Vulcan character Spock in the "Star Trek" franchise, but he also had a long and prolific career otherwise. For example, he directed "Three Men and a Baby," one of the highest-grossing movies of 1987. On top of that, Nimoy published books of photography and continued to act in various roles up until his death in 2015 at the age of 83.
points: Whether Leonard Nimoy was playing a villain of the week or himself in animated form, he made a lot of great supporting appearances in his career.

articles.title: Harry Styles Goes Full Pizza Rat for Halloween at Final MSG Show, Jalen Brunson Makes Surprise Visit
articles.summary: The Hollywood Reporter was inside the arena Saturday night for night two of Styles' traditional "Harryween" concerts, where the musician gave an emotional farewell to his 30-show residency.
body: “I thought I would use this momentous occasion in my career to dress like a rodent,” Harry Styles said Saturday night, explaining his costume for the second night of his traditional “Harryween” concerts.

For night two of Harryween, Styles dressed as “Pizza Rat,” wearing a full rat suit and bringing a pizza slice onstage as an accessory. The costume appeared to take inspiration from the viral 2015 “Pizza Rat” video, which showed a rat dragging a slice of pizza down the stairs of a New York City subway station. Styles fully committed to the look, even playing guitar with his rat-claw nails.

His bandmates also got in on the New York theme, dressing as city landmarks and icons, including the Statue of Liberty, Andy Warhol and Anna Wintour. The previous night’s Harryween concert saw Styles transform into Elvis Presley before changing into the outfit he wore for his 2010 The X Factor UK audition.

articles.title: Author Andy Weir Will Write A Project Hail Mary Sequel Under One Condition [Exclusive]
articles.summary: In a new interview, Project Hail Mary author Andy Weir shares the one thing that has to happen in order for him to write a sequel to his beloved sci-fi novel.
body: Is author Andy Weir ever going to write a sequel to "Project Hail Mary?" That remains to be seen, but he's not opposed to it. Weir just has one very important condition to make it a reality.

With Ryan Gosling in the lead role, the film adaptation of "Project Hail Mary" made enough money at the box office to justify a sequel, pulling in $684 million worldwide. It's also undoubtedly going to be in the awards season conversation. Both Weir's publishing agents and the folks at Amazon MGM Studios would probably love to pull the trigger on a follow-up.

"I would be happy to do a sequel for 'Project Hail Mary' if I got a good idea for one, and I feel like I've had some okay ideas, but not a real good one. I'd rather do no sequel at all than have one that's middling. I'm not going to try to force it, either. I'm not going to go, like, 'I've got to get a sequel idea because in a few years, maybe Ryan won't want to do another movie like this. I've got to get on it.' No. If I come up with a cool idea for a sequel, then I'll workshop it. I'll write it. I'll do all that."

articles.title: 5 Best Western Movies Where The Main Character Dies
articles.summary: Some of the best Western movies ever made end with their leads dying, be they based on real events or early revisionist takes on the Western genre.
body: A common description for a happy ending, that being a hero "riding off into the sunset," comes from Western films. The sunset both bathes the hero in an angelic light and signals a conclusion without being melancholy. Just as the sun will rise again before long, it also suggests the hero will go on to have further adventures and/or a long and happy life, even if the movie never actually receives a sequel.

Named for its gunslinging hero played by Alan Ladd, the 1953 film "Shane" is often ranked as one of the greatest Westerns of all time. It's a mature and solemn Western movie from an era before we started getting harsher deconstructionist Westerns, and it helped set the blueprint for those later films.

articles.title: Romeo + Juliet at 30: how Baz Luhrmann made teens fall in love with Shakespeare
articles.summary: The maximalist, heart over head adaptation of the romantic tragedy made stars of its leads and became an English teacher’s most trusted weapon for Bard-averse students. Romeo + Juliet is not the most renowned or beloved of Shakespeare’s plays, but it is perhaps the most foundational.
body: As such, the blatantly youth-aimed film had plenty of detractors in its time. Critics dismissed it as vulgar and garish, but audiences turned out en masse; Romeo + Juliet made over $147m against a $14.5m budget, boosted in part by a period-defining soundtrack with needle drops from The Cardigans, Everclear, Radiohead and Garbage. (And of course, the song from that oft-replayed fish tank scene, Des’ree’s I’m Kissing You, became the ubiquitous soundtrack for couple-shipping montage videos on 2000s YouTube). By the time I first viewed the film in 2009 – like many, in high school English class, as part of my teacher’s bid to get us invested in Shakespeare – it was already considered a classic.
